As a member of the Airmen Education Physiological Training or Global Survival Training Program for FAA Flight Crew, performs multiple and varying assignments under the limited direction of a team leader or more experienced team member and is responsible for planning, developing, conducting, and evaluating a comprehensive nationwide Physiological Training or Global Survival Training Program for FAA flight crew.

This training is conducted at the Civil Aerospace Medical Institute (CAMI). Applies experience and advanced knowledge to develop lesson plans and training aids; and provides detailed instruction.

Conducts a comprehensive training program in the following areas: Physics of atmosphere, respiration and circulation, hypoxia, hyperventilation, decompression sickness, cabin pressurization and decompression, oxygen equipment operation and usage, smoke mask operation and usage, noise hazards, self-imposed stress, pilot disorientation, drugs, egress and evacuation, night vision, and in survival when the aircraft is in the water, arctic, desert or mountain terrain.

Responsible for keeping current in the latest developments and techniques in civil and military training programs, and incorporating this information into the FAA programs where applicable. Demonstrates considerable independence in planning time and appropriate use of assigned resources to accomplish projects/programs/activities.

On a rotating basis, is responsible for administering and scheduling training. Serves as instructor, operator and/or observer in the low pressure chamber utilized by CAMI, and performs maintenance on such chambers and allied equipment as necessary.

Interviews each trainee to prevent unwarranted chamber reactions because of the trainee's physical condition. Because of the hazardous environment, must recognize life-threatening signs and administer proper and timely response.

Demonstrates the use of various types of oxygen equipment prior to altitude chamber flight and briefs students on safety precautions associated with such equipment. Observes students in the chamber for hypoxia symptoms, hyperventilation, decompression sickness, and ensures all precautions are taken to avoid accidents.

Contacts are internal and external, providing information about the FAA application of procedures as a member of the Airmen Education team.

Lectures in the field of aeromedical education and survival training at accident prevention programs, flight instructor revalidation clinics, pilot examiner clinics, aviation education workshops, flying clubs, aeronautical institutes, aviation departments of colleges and universities, flying schools, air races, air shows, and professional meetings throughout the country.

Consults and advises various FAA departments in matters concerning oxygen equipment configurations, proper oxygen equipment, regulators for crews and passengers, and the various factors of a hostile environment.

Ability to provide consultations and recommendations to individuals and groups involved in special aviation projects concerning aviation physiology and survival situations, including research tasks requiring utilization of low pressure chamber, advising on oxygen equipment configuration, instrumentation readout, interpretation of electronic measurements, and various other components needed to accurately control barometric pressure, humidity, temperature, oxygen concentrations, etc., to accomplish the desired environment necessary for accurate research findings.

Operates training aids such as vertigo producing devices, night vision goggles, oxygen equipment mock-ups, visual illusion devices, life vests, rafts, survival kits, and noise attenuating devices.

Provides guidance, advice, and instruction to industry personnel and private organizations regarding regulations and advisory releases in the field of aviation physiology. Explains FAA policies on physiological training to other members of the agency and the flying public.

Upstream is scaling its use of AI across the organization: in program delivery and practice transformation, partnership success, development, finance, marketing and communications, and within the technology team itself.

Reporting to the Director of Data, Analytics and Technology (DAT), this role is a hands-on, forward-deployed position that will embed directly with teams across Upstream to understand how their work gets done, identify where AI can help (and where it doesn't), build working solutions, and stay with those solutions through adoption and measurement.
This is a manager/builder/coach role: you will discover and prioritize use cases, prototype and deliver practical tools, and develop the training and resources that raise AI fluency organization-wide, all while leading tool evaluations, guardrails, and cost stewardship that keep our AI footprint responsible and sustainable.

Use Case Discovery & Prioritization
Embed with teams across Upstream to understand end-to-end workflows, undocumented processes, and the manual work that slows them down.
Identify, scope, and prioritize AI and automation opportunities based on business impact, feasibility, adoption potential, and risk.
Translate ambiguous business problems into clearly defined use cases, solution hypotheses, and build plans.
Exercise judgment about what is worth building — including recommending against AI when a simpler process change or an existing tool solves the problem.
Solution Building & Delivery
Design, build, test, and deploy practical AI-enabled solutions — prompts, skills, agents, automations, and lightweight applications — using Upstream's approved AI tools, platforms and enterprise data.
Prototype rapidly, put working solutions in front of real users quickly, and iterate based on feedback and observed usage.
Build and curate a reusable library of prompts, skills, templates, and workflow components so that solutions compound rather than live in one person's hands.
Partner with DAT colleagues to transition validated prototypes into supported, production-ready solutions when scale or sensitivity warrants it.
Document solution requirements, configurations, operating procedures, and expected outcomes.
Enablement, Training & Adoption
In collaboration with other DAT team members, develop and deliver Upstream's AI training program — workshops, office hours, self-paced content, and role-specific guidance — so Upstreamers across every function use AI effectively, safely, and confidently.
Create and maintain user-facing resources including documentation, quick-start guides, best practices, and the Upstream AI Hub.
Cultivate a network of AI champions across departments who drive adoption within their own teams.
Surface and share wins — quantified time savings, before/after workflows, and lessons learned — to build organizational momentum.
Support change management for new AI tools and ways of working, meeting people where they are and building trust with skeptics as well as enthusiasts.
Governance, Tools & Measurement
Serve as Upstream's internal subject matter expert across our evolving AI and automation ecosystem.
Evaluate emerging AI tools, platforms, and connectors; recommend what to adopt, pilot, or decline, in partnership with DAT leadership.
Partner with DAT, Finance, and Contracts colleagues on license administration, provisioning, vendor review, cost tracking, and renewal planning for AI tools.
Help establish and maintain practical guardrails covering data privacy, PHI and sensitive-data handling, appropriate use, and human review — and educate Upstreamers on them.
Define and track success metrics tied to real outcomes: time saved, quality improvements, usage, and adoption; report progress to DAT and organizational leadership.
